items.title: Before the first guest
items.summary: The safety checks a holiday home in England needs, and who does what.
body: GOV.UK sets out what an owner letting a self-catering holiday home in England is responsible for. Fire safety comes first: a fire risk assessment for the home, with smoke and carbon monoxide alarms where they're needed.

Gas appliances need a check every year by a Gas Safe registered engineer, and electrical equipment has to be kept safe. We arrange the checks with you before the first booking, and keep the dates in your file.
A national register of short-term lets in England is coming. GOV.UK says it is expected to begin in March 2027; it is not in force yet. We'll register the homes we look after when it opens.

sources.label: GOV.UK: letting out a self-catering holiday home in England

items.title: If your home is in London, Wales or Scotland
items.summary: Ninety nights in London, a licence in Scotland, a register in Wales.
body: In Greater London, a home can be let for short stays for up to 90 nights a year without planning permission, and whoever lets it must pay its council tax. The rule is in section 44 of the Deregulation Act 2015.
In Scotland, every short-term let needs a licence from the local council before it takes bookings or guests.
In Wales, anyone taking bookings for overnight stays must register with the Welsh Revenue Authority by 31 March 2027. Registration is free. Councils may also add a Visitor Levy.
